questions.question: How do scientists calculate global surface temperatures to track climate trends?
options: By averaging tens of thousands of measurements taken worldwide.
By using a single ultra-precise thermometer at the equator.
By estimating temperature based entirely on satellite photos of ice caps.
By taking measurements from just ten major cities once a year.

questions.question: What trend has been observed in overall global surface temperatures since the industrial revolution in the 1850s?
options: They have remained completely stable with no notable changes.
They have been steadily decreasing.
They have been increasing overall.
They have fluctuated with no long-term directional trend.

questions.question: Which of the following can scientists use to obtain data about longer-term historical changes in Earth's temperature before modern records?
options: Fossilized bones of dinosaurs and modern soil samples.
Tree rings and ice cores.
Active volcanic ash deposits and ocean wave heights.
Current satellite measurements and tectonic plate speeds.

questions.question: How does methane compare to carbon dioxide as a greenhouse gas?
options: Methane is a more potent greenhouse gas than carbon dioxide.
Methane is much less potent at trapping heat than carbon dioxide.
Methane and carbon dioxide have exactly the same potency.
Methane does not trap heat at all, unlike carbon dioxide.

questions.question: What is the primary effect of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere on Earth's climate?
options: They make the atmosphere significantly colder than it would be without them.
They keep the atmosphere warmer than it would be without them.
They prevent any heat from the Sun from reaching the surface.
They keep the temperature of the atmosphere at absolute zero.

questions.question: How does the melting of land-based ice sheets due to increased temperatures affect global oceans?
options: It moves more water into the sea, causing sea levels to rise.
It has no effect on sea levels because the ice is already floating.
It causes sea levels to fall because water becomes denser as it cools.
It decreases the total volume of water in the global oceans.

questions.question: What is the effect of sea ice melting during the summer on global sea levels?
options: It drastically raises sea levels because it adds liquid water to the ocean.
It lowers sea levels because liquid water takes up less space than ice.
It does not add water to the sea or raise sea levels.
It permanently decreases the temperature of the deep ocean, raising sea levels.

questions.question: Why does the warming of oceans and seas contribute to rising sea levels?
options: Warmer water contracts, leaving more space for rainwater.
Warmer water expands, causing the volume of the seas to increase.
Warm water evaporates faster, which directly pushes the coastlines outward.
Warmer water becomes heavier, pressing down on the seabed to push the water up.

questions.question: Why might an electric vehicle still indirectly contribute to greenhouse gas emissions?
options: Because electric vehicles release greenhouse gases directly from their tailpipes while driving.
Because fuels may be burned at power stations to generate the electricity they use.
Because electric vehicles require constant burning of fuel inside their batteries.
Because electric vehicles emit large amounts of methane gas from their tyres.

questions.question: What is the process involved in carbon capture and storage?
options: It releases CO₂ into the upper atmosphere to be destroyed by solar radiation.
It converts CO₂ into oxygen gas using artificial outdoor forests.
It separates CO₂ from other emissions and stores it in suitable deep underground locations.
It mixes CO₂ with surface ocean water to increase its acidity and lock it away.

questions.question: What is a major disadvantage of carbon capture and storage technology despite its ability to reduce CO₂ emissions?
options: It is very expensive to implement and operate.
It actually increases the total amount of CO₂ released.
It can only be used in domestic households and not in factories.
It makes the stored carbon dioxide highly radioactive.

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of global greenhouse gas emissions is produced by the energy sector?
Which of the following factors will cause a car to use more energy to travel a distance of 100 km?
options: If the car is heavier or travels at higher speeds.
If the car is lighter or travels at lower speeds.
If the car is painted a lighter color.
If the car is driven only during the daytime.

questions.question: How can maintaining the correct air pressure in a car's tyres affect its energy usage?
options: It increases the energy used because the tyres become heavier.
It has no effect whatsoever on energy use.
It reduces the energy used by the car.
It forces the engine to burn more fuel to spin the wheels.

questions.question: Why will renewable energy resources not run out?
options: Because they are replenished more quickly than we use them up.
Because they do not use any physical materials to generate electricity.
Because they are stored in infinite underground reservoirs.
Because they are made from recycled plastics.

questions.question: How do solar panels differ from many other common methods of electricity generation?
options: They use falling water to turn small internal gears.
They produce electricity without using electric generators.
They require burning biomass at high temperatures to function.
They must spin a giant turbine to generate an electric current.
